description: Multi-turn session (issue #23): two assistant turns in one session_id. Turn 1 writes notes.txt; turn 2 (resumed via `claude -p --continue`) edits it. Each turn ends with its own Stop hook, and events continue after the first Stop — the canary for 'Stop fires per-turn, not per-session'.
notes: Captured with a two-prompt headless run: `claude -p <turn1>` then `claude -p --continue <turn2>`, both pointing the SessionStart/UserPromptSubmit/PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Stop hooks at one append-only dump. The `--continue` resume emits a second SessionStart with source=resume (a genuine, observed upstream behavior), so the same session_id carries two turns. The load-bearing fact for liveness (issue #23) is the mid-stream Stop at index 4 followed by more events: a live session reads live mid-turn and idle between turns, never terminally stopped.
